ratings.reviewer_notes: DR-focused review links VEGF overexpression to neovascularization and vascular permeability and discusses interaction with Ang-2/Tie2, inflammation, and oxidative stress.
Describes complementary VEGF and Tie2 regulation of angiogenesis, permeability, and inflammation, but covers several retinal vascular diseases rather than DR specifically.
Provides relevant VEGFR2 downstream mechanisms, including PLC-PKC-MAPK signaling and TSAd-dependent migration, but is a general VEGFR2 review with only limited DR-specific treatment.

Directly reviews how diabetic ischemia, oxidative stress, and PKC activation increase VEGF, leading to angiogenesis, endothelial permeability, altered apoptosis, and inflammatory mediator activation in DR.

In a DR mouse model, electrical stimulation suppresses VEGF-A expression, leakage, microaneurysms, inflammation, and angiogenic behavior, but the principal mechanism studied is metabolic modulation rather than VEGF signaling itself.
PDR-focused experiments show reciprocal CD146/VEGF regulation and connect sCD146-induced ERK, NF-kB, VEGF, and MMP-9 activation to endothelial migration and retinal vascular permeability.
Establishes VEGF as a cytokine and permeability factor in DME and discusses anti-VEGF response, but primarily reviews non-VEGF mechanisms and targets.
Reviews experimental and clinical evidence establishing VEGF as a causal driver of vascular permeability and angiogenesis in DR and DME.
Directly reviews VEGF interactions with COX-2/prostaglandin and nitric oxide pathways in diabetic retinal barrier breakdown, vascular permeability, angiogenesis, and neurodegeneration.
Comparative clinical trial of three anti-VEGF agents reports visual outcomes and treatment frequency but does not investigate mechanisms linking VEGF signaling to DR progression.
DR-focused review covers mechanisms increasing retinal VEGF and cytokine expression and links VEGF to vascular dysfunction, permeability, edema, and angiogenesis.

Identifies a MEK-pERK-FosB/DeltaFosB-VCAM-1 axis affecting retinal permeability and angiogenesis and tests VEGF-induced leakage, but uses non-diabetic injury and VEGF-administration models rather than DR progression.
Provides adjacent DR context on inflammation, permeability, neovascularization, and anti-VEGF therapy, but focuses mainly on inflammatory mechanisms and treatments rather than VEGF signaling.

Reviews TGF-beta1 interaction with VEGF and Smad, MAPK, PI3K/Akt, Wnt, and NF-kB pathways contributing to pathological angiogenesis, permeability, barrier disruption, fibrosis, and inflammation in DR.
PDR experiments link hypoxia-induced MIF/CD74 signaling to ERK activation and VEGF production, vascular permeability, adhesion molecules, and retinal endothelial migration and proliferation.

DR models show that combined Cx43 silencing and anti-VEGF treatment reduces VEGF expression, angiogenesis, permeability, inflammation, and apoptosis, but the study emphasizes delivery and therapeutic synergy rather than VEGF pathway mechanisms.
Directly reviews VEGFR1 signaling in retinal endothelial, glial, and inflammatory cells and its effects on permeability and production of proinflammatory and proangiogenic mediators relevant to DR.

PDR-focused mechanistic study shows reciprocal VEGF/CD40 regulation and links CD40L-CD40 activation to ERK/NF-kB signaling, VEGF induction, vascular permeability, adhesion molecules, and endothelial proliferation and migration.

Directly examines VEGF expression in human nonproliferative DR but finds no diabetes-associated increase, suggesting constitutive retinal VEGF expression rather than a demonstrated progression mechanism.
PDR study shows abnormal hyaluronan metabolism activates ERK/NF-kB and increases VEGF, Ang-2, and inflammatory mediators, alongside vascular permeability and endothelial migration.
Directly reviews VEGF-A signaling through VEGFR1 and VEGFR2 in DR, including hypoxic regulation, mitogenic signaling, increased vascular permeability, and pathological neovascularization.
